data.name: Jairaj
data.gender_notes: Jairaj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jai: victory, Raja: ruler. This name is derived from the Sanskrit language and is a powerful name for a boy. It conveys the idea of a brave and victorious leader. The name Jairaj carries the meaning “Victorious Ruler” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jairaj usually hope their child will grow to embody victorious ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: May the blessings of the gods grant you victory and leadership.
data.etymology: Jairaj belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victorious Ruler.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jairaj total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jairaj is rooted in the rich cultural heritage of Hinduism. It embodies the values of strength, courage, and victory. A name like Jairaj inspires bravery, resilience, and determination, qualities that have been celebrated in Hindu mythology, literature, and folklore for centuries.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Jairaj lies in its connection to the divine. It symbolizes the inner warrior that strives for victory over the fears and obstacles of life. This name is a reminder that every individual has the inner strength and courage to overcome challenges and achieve success. It is also a reflection of the Hindu belief in Karma, the law of cause and effect, and the idea that victory is not just a matter of luck, but is earned through effort and determination. Thus, the name Jairaj represents both the material and spiritual aspects of human life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jairaj: Radiant Victory, triumphant and victorious, shimmering with inner light and victory over self.

historical_references.context: Jairaj was a king of the Rashtrakut Dynasty, ruling from around 818 to 834 CE. He was a successor of Dharavarshan I and is known for his campaigns against the Pallava and Chalukya dynasties. He is also known for his patronage of the arts and architecture, particularly the cave temples at Ellora.
